chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
The one in Ihram steps aside from the locusts when they are on the road, so if he has no alternative, he kills them, and there is no penalty upon him.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on killing locusts while in Ihram?
ai.summary: Reported by Zurarah, a prominent Imamite scholar, this hadith clarifies the principle of *bara'ah* (exemption from penalty) in cases of necessity (*darurah*) during Ihram. It distinguishes between the general prohibition of killing land game and the specific dispensation for locusts when they obstruct the path, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on ease and the absence of fault when avoidance is impossible.
